Hi -- glad you are working with it!  Sorry for the complexity!  


On Sat, Oct 28, 2017 at 3:52 AM, XXX wrote:
Hi Nick,

I am having some issues trying to get a BioGeoBEARS analysis to run and was wondering if you could give me some feedback. Basically, I am getting an error message saying that some tip ranges are not allowed according to the states_list. I have tried using a custom states_list which defines all allowed ranges, but that does not seem to solve the problem either.

An area_adjacency matrix will limit the state space -- meaning, limit the list of allowed ranges.  Another thing that will limit the list of allowed states/ranges is the max_range_size setting, if max_range_size=4, then any ranges with more than 4 areas are disallowed. If you then had a tip in the tipranges/geography file with 5 areas, you would get that area.

I suspect your problem is something simple, like having uncommented the area_adjacency line, but then forgetting to re-comment-it-out when you use a different strategy like the custom ranges list.  

You probably saw this, but it gives some advice -- I would recommend the custom modification of the ranges list, then you know exactly what you are doing:
http://phylo.wikidot.com/biogeobears#areas_adjacency_matrix2



Here is an example of what happens: I am working on a global scale and have defined an area adjacency matrix of the major terrestrial zoogeographic realms. I have allowed for a connection between the Palearctic and Nearctic (via Beringia), but the Sino-Japanese region is only adjacent to the Palearctic. However, it is of course perfectly conceivable (I think) to potentially have a range that includes all three areas, but that does not seem to be allowed according to my adjacency matrix.

Maybe I am missing something blatantly obvious, but I can't seem to figure this out (even when specifying my custom states_list). Any suggestions on how to fix this?

You should be able to do the custom states list, then look at your states_list or ranges_list and see whether or not e.g. Palearctic+Neartic+Sino-Japan is in that list -- that's the key thing.

Cheers!
Nick
